title: Margin % on an invoice row uses only that row's side
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • You are signed in as a user with the "Admin" role at {Location-A}.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • Two active staff members at {Location-A} have their "Sales Representative" switch on: {Sales-rep-A} and {Sales-rep-B}.
    For example: {Sales-rep-A} is ZZAUTOTEST Ann Able and {Sales-rep-B} is ZZAUTOTEST Ben Able.
  • Customer {Customer-A} has no sales representative.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST SSR Fleet.
  • {Location-A}'s Shop Supplies Charge is 0%, and nothing else is invoiced at {Location-A} today.
  • Work order {Work-order-1} for {Customer-A} is open and not invoiced; it has one labor line of 2.00 hours at $100.00 an hour and one part with cost $30.00 sold at $50.00; Labor reads {Sales-rep-A} and Parts reads {Sales-rep-B}.
    For example: {Work-order-1} is S2-40001.
  • Starting screen: {Work-order-1} is open in a desktop browser at least 1024 px wide.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Invoice {Work-order-1}.
  2. Open Reports > Sales By Representative, set the date range to today, turn Show Unassigned on and turn the Sales Type column on in the column selector.
  3. Read the Parts row's Parts Margin and Margin %.
  4. Read the Labor row's Labor Invoiced, Labor Margin and Margin %.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the invoice is created.
  • Step 2: two rows show for the invoice.
  • Step 3: Parts Margin $20.00 and Margin % 40.00% (20 ÷ 50 × 100); labor plays no part.
  • Step 4: Margin % equals Labor Margin ÷ $200.00 × 100, from the labor figures only.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Splitting Sales Representatives", Confluence 919928833, version 11 (21 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 22 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10890, story SV-11269 (Story 5, Credit each side on the invoice and in Sales By Representative)

  • S5-R17: “On an invoice row, the Margin % uses only the side the row is credited with.”
